beats.narration_text: A model with fifty inputs is rarely a model with fifty real signals. L1 regularization does something Ridge cannot: it removes features outright. This is Liam, in for Bear. Lasso shrinks the weights, and then it sets some of them to exactly zero, making the fit and a feature-selection decision in one move. Let us see why the geometry forces that.

show.event: Claude composer opens; greeting 'Ciao, Liam'
the ask types in: why does L1 zero coefficients out
send arms; running text reads 'pricing the weights…'
answered lines land: shrink / exactly zero / selection built in

props.command: Explain L1 regularization (Lasso). Show why penalizing total absolute weight drives some coefficients to exactly zero, while the squared penalty only makes them small.
output: fitting and feature selection in one

beats.narration_text: Here is the whole idea in one breath. L1 regularization adds a second bill to the fitting problem: the total absolute size of the coefficients. Paying that bill pulls every weight toward zero, and because of the shape of the penalty, some weights arrive at exactly zero. Those features drop out of the model entirely. You get a simpler model and a shortlist, from one setting.

show.event: spark line: 'Shrink some. Zero others.'
five coefficient bars grow to their unpenalised lengths
every bar shortens as the penalty is applied
two bars collapse to nothing; their values turn terracotta 0.00
footer lands: 'two features removed — not just reduced'

production_viz.label: shrink and select
production_viz.mechanic: coefficients shrink; two land on exactly zero and leave the model

beats.narration_text: The machinery is one objective with two jobs. Start with the prediction error on the training data. Then add lambda times the total absolute weight, every coefficient's magnitude, summed. Lambda at zero is ordinary least squares. Raise lambda and each unit of weight costs more, so the optimizer has to justify every coefficient it keeps. Same fit, now on a budget.

show.event: spark line: 'One score. Two jobs.'
DATA FIT card appears — squared error
plus sign, then the L1 PENALTY card — lambda × total absolute weight
arrow drops into one MINIMIZE card: the sum of both
footer lands: 'more penalty → simpler model'

production_viz.label: the penalised objective
production_viz.mechanic: error plus lambda times summed absolute weight, minimised together

beats.narration_text: Why exactly zero, and not merely small? Picture the budget as a region the solution has to stay inside. Squaring gives you a circle, smooth everywhere, so the best point almost never sits on an axis. Absolute value gives you a diamond, and a diamond has corners sitting right on the axes. The loss contours tend to meet that corner first, and at a corner one coefficient is precisely zero.

show.event: spark line: 'The corner is everything.'
two headers set the comparison: L1 absolute value vs L2 squared value
the L1 diamond and the L2 circle draw on over their axes
terracotta loss contours arrive and touch each region
contact dots mark where: a corner on the left, a smooth arc on the right
captions land: 'meets a corner → exactly zero' vs 'meets a smooth edge → just small'

production_viz.label: diamond versus circle
production_viz.mechanic: the L1 constraint region has axis corners; the L2 region does not
production_viz.note: schematic geometry — contours are illustrative, not fitted

beats.narration_text: Now sweep the penalty and watch. At a small lambda every predictor keeps a weight. Turn it up and the weakest one hits zero and leaves. Turn it further and the next one goes. This is the regularization path, and it is the honest picture of what Lasso does. Not a ranking. A sequence of removals, one threshold at a time.

show.event: spark line: 'Watch them drop out.'
axes draw on; four named coefficients label the left margin
four paths trace downward as the penalty grows
terracotta dots mark each arrival at exactly zero
note lands: 'each one lands on exactly zero'

production_viz.label: regularization path
production_viz.mechanic: coefficients reach zero at different penalty strengths, one at a time

beats.narration_text: So which lambda? Do not eyeball it. Hold out data, sweep the penalty, and plot validation error. It falls as you cut variance, then climbs once you start deleting real signal. Take the bottom of that curve. And standardize your features first, because the penalty compares raw coefficient magnitudes, so an unscaled variable gets charged the wrong price.

show.event: spark line: 'Tune it. Don't guess.'
axes draw on with a rotated 'validation error' label
the U-shaped validation curve traces out
terracotta dot marks the minimum; a dashed line drops to the axis
'lowest validation error' lands with small/large penalty ends
footer: 'standardize features first'

production_viz.label: cross-validated lambda
production_viz.mechanic: validation error is U-shaped in the penalty; the minimum is the choice

beats.narration_text: Now the cleanup, because sparsity flatters itself. Give Lasso two correlated features and it keeps one and drops its twin, nearly arbitrarily. Resample the data and the surviving subset changes, so do not read that list as discovery. The survivors are biased too, pulled toward zero. And selected never means causal. Elastic net exists precisely because grouped predictors break this.

show.event: spark line: 'Where sparsity lies.'
CORRELATED TWINS tile: keeps one, drops its twin
UNSTABLE PICKS tile: resample, get a new subset
SHRINKAGE BIAS tile: survivors are pulled down
NOT CAUSATION tile: selected is not the same as true

production_viz.label: four failure modes
production_viz.mechanic: correlated twins, unstable selection, shrinkage bias, no causal claim
production_viz.note: qualitative failure modes, not measured rates

beats.narration_text: The verdict. L1 regularization penalizes total absolute weight, which shrinks every coefficient and drives some of them to exactly zero. That makes it a fitting method and a feature selector at once. Choose lambda by cross-validation, standardize before you fit, and treat the selected set as one plausible subset rather than the truth. Ridge shrinks. Lasso decides.

show.event: artifact board opens: 'Shrink, then select'
SHRINK row fills: every weight pulled toward zero
SELECT row fills: some weights land exactly on zero
TUNE row fills: cross-validate lambda, scale first
CHECK row fills: correlated picks stay unstable

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Paste this in: fit Lasso across a range of penalties on your own data, plot the regularization path, and mark where each coefficient reaches zero. Then refit on a bootstrap resample and compare which features survive. That second half is the part people skip, and it is the part that tells you whether your shortlist is a finding or an accident. Watch how much the survivor list moves.

beats.narration_text: L1 regularization, oversimplified. Ridge makes weights small. Lasso makes choices, so audit the choices. Liam, in for Bear.
